plants.name: Aster novi-belgii
plants.description: A clump-forming perennial native to eastern North America that produces masses of daisy-like flowers with yellow centers. It is a vital late-season nectar source for migrating monarch butterflies and native bees, and it is widely cultivated in gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Eastern North America; cultivated worldwide in temperate gardens
plants.funFact: The genus name Aster comes from the Greek word for 'star', and in the Victorian language of flowers asters symbolized patience and love.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulbous perennial whose crocus-like flowers emerge from bare ground in autumn, long after its leaves have died back. It grows in damp meadows and woodland edges and is also planted in gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to mid autumn (September to October)
plants.location: Europe, from the British Isles to central Europe; naturalized elsewhere
plants.funFact: Despite its name it is not a true crocus. It is highly toxic, yet it is the source of colchicine, a compound used in medicine and in plant breeding to double chromosome numbers.

plants.name: Prunus serrulata
plants.commonName: Japanese Flowering Cherry (Spring-blooming in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.description: Ornamental cherry trees cover themselves in clouds of blossom as spring arrives in the Southern Hemisphere. In places like Australia, New Zealand and Chile, mid to late September is peak bloom for cultivated cherry varieties.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (September to October)
plants.location: Cultivated in southern Australia, New Zealand, South Africa and Chile; native to Japan, China and Korea
plants.funFact: Cherry blossom viewing, or hanami, has been a Japanese tradition for over a thousand years, and Southern Hemisphere cities now hold their own cherry blossom festivals in September.

plants.name: Lycoris radiata
plants.description: A striking bulbous plant whose leafless stalks shoot up in early autumn, topped with bright red flowers that have long, curling stamens. It is often seen blooming along rice paddies and in cemeteries in East Asia.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to mid autumn (September to October)
plants.location: China, Korea and Japan; naturalized in the southeastern United States
plants.funFact: In Japan it blooms around the autumn equinox, a time called Higan, so it is known as Higanbana, the flower of the equinox.
